questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew absolutely nothing about the host uni. I chose only based of the partner unis of ucph within countries where I partly knew the language. And then picked a smaller town than the capital, thinking it would be easier to socialize with locals in a smaller town.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a lot of fun and I learned a lot. What was still missing for me was that I didn't realise that most exchange people arrived 3-4 weeks before me, and most of the social events where already done. So I did feel like I missed out on some social events due to unclear information on semesterstart and introduction for internationals.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was moderately difficult. I had a lot of trouble communicating with my contact at the host uni, and the informations about courses, documents needed and housing was difficult to find and had pretty unclear information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We were invited to orientation days, but then told that there would be no orientation for medical students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got it through the university. It was a fairly easy process, but very short term answer. I got confirmation of accomodation less than a week before arrival.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is great, because it forces you to get out of campus and see the city around you. I lived in student accomodation and thus with other students, even though i didn't live on campus, so I still got a lot of social activity through my student housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: communication with the student housing was difficult and the facilities worn down and outdated. But overall nice location and affordable.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't remember having any problems with it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: as far as I remember I just had to fill out one page with infos about A4 format. And that was it

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I have no idea. I didn't experience any problems and didn't look for help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty succesful. I was informed upon arrival that one course I registered for would not be available, but was then offered an alternative course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The official registration process is not the problem. The problem is arranging clinical courses with the contact person at the medical faculty. She does not always answer her mails and is generally unhelpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They lived up to the requirements of my home uni. The courses did not exceed expectations but they did what they needed to do

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had clinical courses. I felt that they were generally at a slightly lower level than at ucph. But being a bit proactive and asking to do more brought me through at an acceptable level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We were much less independant at my host uni than at ucph. Much more classical teaching in my exchange, where we got lectures and quizzes from senior doctors. At ucph I feel we get to learn by doing more often, which I like better.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
clinical course of Internal Medicine (endocrinology)
clinical course of Surgery (visceral surgery)
clinical course of Anesthesiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since these are the only courses available at this semester, probably the same. I would definitely recommend visceral surgery! for internal medicine I don't think it matters that much which specialty you choose.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: the semester fee of a 110 eur. I did not expect to have to pay to the uni. But I have had a lot of use of the transport benefits and the canteen that these money go to.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Generally I expected to be paying more for food and housing. So there I was positively surprised

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was here for a very short time, so none of the opportunities made sense for me to participate in. But they looked to be good and easily accesible

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: sports and choir that I heard about. Probably also an orchestra. A lot of differents sports available

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend doing some of the sports during the semester. It is a good way to meet new people, both local and international.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: As much as possible! Definitely go to Strasbourg and see that. Go to the other historic towns in the neighbourhood. Go hiking in the amazing nature! Go to the city-festivals!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Coming from another northern european country I did not have a lot of difficulties fitting in. The only thing maybe being that it was difficult to get used to using cash everywhere. And that nothing in Germany is digitalised.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports or choir. Take classes in german. Do not be afraid to take the initiative to talk to the local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the absense of digitalisation and the overall use of cash

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found the germans more open towards foreigners, than I know danes to be

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring cash! Take the german course offered by uni heidelberg. take german courses and don't be afraid to approach germans.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need all your documents printed out.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing how much my language has improved and how my confidence has grown in speaking german.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably planning the exchange

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
